orphanDialog: penny|Halt. Neighborhood Watch. State your business.
penny|I know who you are. You water your drought garden. Everybody knows.
penny|Bernadette. Neighborhood Watch Captain, nineteen years. And I'll say it, because nobody else will.
penny|The squirrels are organized.
penny|They have lookouts in the playground, a spy in the community garden,
penny|and somebody at the picnic tables stuffing their cheeks with anything that's not nailed down.
penny|Everything they steal goes up THAT tree, the Old Oak. There's a little door in the trunk that opens with a secret knock. I've only ever heard bits of it.
penny|Clear the squirrels out of those three spots, and Nara can dig up what they buried. I'd bet a piece of that secret knock is in each hole.
penny|I'll be here with my clipboard.
penny|Neighborhood Watch Captain’s report: case closed.
penny|I'd like it noted that I was right.
penny|And these. Neighborhood Watch Vests. I give out one every nineteen years. Today I'm giving out three. Even the dog.
penny|Bernadette. Neighborhood Watch Captain, nineteen years. Nothing gets past me.
penny|Except squirrels. I'm working on it.
penny|The lookouts first. Playground, garden, picnic tables. Then Nara digs.
penny|Then the tree. There's a knock. I have only ever heard parts of it.
penny|Case closed. I've filed my report. With myself. I approved it.
penny|I said they were organized. Nobody believed me. Write that down.
penny|You're a good neighbor, Tom. So is the dog. Mostly the dog.
tnb|Babe, she has a corkboard with red string. I've never felt so seen.
tnb|Noted. On a corkboard. With red string.
